chunks: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: It is related in the narration that when he (peace be upon him) delivered this sermon, the skins trembled, the eyes wept, and the hearts quaked.
And some people call this sermon 'Al-Gharrā' (the Brilliant).

key_terms.الْغَرَّاءُ: The Brilliant (a title for a specific sermon)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the title 'Al-Gharrā' in relation to Imam Ali's sermon?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi highlights the visceral impact of Imam Ali's oratory, where the listeners' physical trembling and weeping attest to the sermon's power to pierce the heart, a phenomenon often attributed to the divine eloquence (balagha) characteristic of the Ahl al-Bayt. The title 'Al-Gharrā' (the Brilliant) signifies the sermon's role as a guiding light, emphasizing its function not merely as speech but as a transformative spiritual event that instills deep piety (taqwa) in the audience.
